name: Fenris Ashwood
equipment: An insignia of rank (mercenary company badge)
A trophy taken from a fallen enemy (a troll tooth on a leather cord)
features: Relentless Endurance (drop to 1 HP instead of 0 HP, 1/long rest)
Savage Attacks (extra damage die on critical melee hits)
Fighting Style: Defense (+1 AC while wearing armor)
Second Wind (bonus action, regain 1d10+3 HP, 1/short rest)
Action Surge (take one additional action, 1/short rest)
Military Rank (Soldier feature: soldiers recognize your authority)

personality.traits: I am slow to speak but when I do, people listen. I have a dry, dark sense of humor that surfaces at the worst possible moments.
personality.ideals: Pragmatism. The world is not fair, and idealism gets people killed. Do the job, get paid, survive.
personality.bonds: My mercenary company, the Ashwood Axes, was wiped out on a contract gone wrong. I am the last survivor, and I carry the company standard — a burned axe on a grey field — in their memory.
personality.flaws: I trust gold more than words, and my cynicism pushes people away. I take too many risks because some part of me does not expect — or want — to survive my companions.

appearance: A towering half-orc standing 6'4" with dusky green-grey skin and a heavy, muscular build that speaks of a lifetime of violence. His black hair is cropped close to his skull, and his lower canines protrude slightly, giving his resting expression a perpetual scowl. A web of old scars covers his forearms, and his knuckles are thick with calluses. He carries himself with the watchful economy of movement of a professional soldier — no wasted energy, no unnecessary gestures. His chain mail is functional and unadorned, the metal darkened to reduce reflection in underground environments.
backstory: Fenris grew up on the streets of Waterdeep, the bastard son of a human tavern keeper and an orc mercenary he never met. He found his place in the Ashwood Axes, a mercenary company that valued competence over lineage, and spent fifteen years fighting in every conflict from border skirmishes to dungeon clearances. When the company took a contract to escort a merchant caravan through the Underdark, they were ambushed by drow slavers. Fenris was the only survivor, left for dead among the bodies of his companions. He fought his way back to the surface alone, carrying the company standard and a burning desire for revenge against the drow who destroyed his family. The Underdark expedition offers a paycheck and a chance to settle that debt.
